SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: Participants were divided into low- (n = 45, M = 6.7, SD = 3.9)and high- (n = 41, M = 27.0, SD = 11.3) creative achievement groups by CAQ score median split. Members of the low-creative achievement group in the preexposed condition (n = 28) scored significantly higher on the LI task than the low-creative achievers in the nonpreexposed condition (n = 17), indicating a significant LI effect. Members of the high-creative achievement group in the preexposed condition (n = 29), by contrast, did not score significantly higher on the LI task than their counterparts in the nonpreexposed condition (n = 12). As hypothesized, the mean LI score of the low-creative achievement group (n=28, M=21.8, SD=10.4) was significantly higher than that of the high-creative achievement group (n=29, M=14.3, SD=8.8) in the preexposed condition.

section_summary.extract_value: This section details a study investigating the relationship between creative achievement, measured by CAQ, and Latent Inhibition (LI). Participants were categorized into low- (n=45) and high- (n=41) creative achievement groups based on a CAQ score median split. The study found a significant LI effect in the low-creative achievement group (n=28 in preexposed, n=17 in nonpreexposed), but this effect was attenuated in the high-creative achievement group (n=29 in preexposed, n=12 in nonpreexposed). An ANOVA confirmed significant differences in LI scores attributable to creative achievement levels, with the low-creative achievement group showing significantly higher mean LI scores in the preexposed condition compared to the high-creative achievement group.
